# Bala Saṁyutta (SN 50)
**ID:** SN 50
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Bala Saṁyutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn50
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Rather than featuring distinctive narrative settings or interlocutors, the texts apply stock imagery—such as the river Ganges sloping and inclining toward the east—to depict the cultivation of the five powers as slanting and inclining toward Nibbāna, sharing these programmatic similes and formulas with other sections of the *Mahāvagga* [Bodhi 2003; Polak 2011].
In comparative studies, Choong has noted that not a single discourse is shared between the *Bala-saṁyukta* of the Chinese SĀ and the Pali *Bala Saṁyutta*, indicating that both traditions separately felt the need to construct a collection around the powers to complete the standard sets of bodhipakkhiyādhammā [Analayo 2014].
Text-reuse computations from DharmaNexus highlight this formulaic character, registering 843 Pali-internal reuse passages across 22 collections, predominantly matching the parallel repetition series of the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46), and *Indriya Saṁyutta* (SN 48), as well as thematic matches in the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text automatically with the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and Chinese and Tibetan canonical parallels [DharmaNexus].
